newsitem.title: FINLAND: Niinisto sees Finnish EMU deficit at zero in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Niinisto sees Finnish EMU deficit at zero in 1998.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday that the deficit of the Finnish public sector finances, the so called EMU deficit, would narrow to zero in 1997 from about 1.5 percent of GDP projected this year.

Speaking at a seminar, Niinisto also said Finnish GDP growth would accelerate to between four and five percent this year and that the finance ministry would revise its unemployment rate forecasts lower.
"The deficit of the public sector, that is the EMU deficit, will narrow to zero during next year," Niinisto said.

"In the state finances, there will still be a distinct deficit. We will be lucky if we manage to squeeze it to around 20 billion markka ($4 billion)," he said. This year's deficit in state finances is projected at about 28.5 billion markka.
"We see GDP growth in the region of four to five percent this year," Niinisto said.
The finance ministry's economics department is scheduled to publish a new economic forecast on February 18. Its previous forecast, from September 1996, saw 3.9-percent growth in 1997.
"The finance ministry intends to revise its unemployment rate forecast to below 15 percent for this year and below 14 percent in 1998," Niinisto said.
Last September, the ministry projected an average 1997 jobless rate of 15.4 percent.
